text: Is it bad if young guys get into a serious relationship with the very first girl they start seeing? Or should they explore first, get some experience, and figure out what actually works for them? And what about women? Is it bad for them to get experience first before settling down? I partly talked about this in one of my dating questions from subscribers videos. And I received a disapproving, emotionally charged comment from a woman. Here it is. Don't listen to this dude. He is basically telling guys not to get serious with the first girl and saying it is good for guys to explore first, but at the same time saying girls who want to explore are red flags. Make it make sense. So let me start with a simple question. Where exactly did I say that a girl who wants to explore is a red flag? My guess is this lady just assumed it, believed the version she created in her head, and went ahead to write emotionally charged comments. But thank you for this comment, miss, because it gave me an idea to make this video, where I clarify why I think young men should first get experience, go on many dates, seduce certain number of women, experience some situations, and only then get into a serious relationship. And is it the same for women? Now let me start with this. I am not saying serious relationships are bad. I'm saying that to get into a good, healthy relationship, you first need to know what works for you and what doesn't. You need to have criteria. And that normally comes with experience. Not just any experience, but valuable and hard-earned dating experience. And in my world, both men and women need experience before going into a serious relationship. But what counts as valuable and hard-earned experience is a bit different. In today's world, most women don't lack attention from men. If a woman installs dating apps, she can get hundreds or even thousands of likes. If she's active on social media, her inbox can be full of DMs. If she has a social life, guys would probably approach to get to know her. Attention is not a scarce resource for most women. Because of that, you can think of a young woman as an HR manager. She has many candidates. Getting options isn't hard. What actually matters and what takes real experience is knowing how to choose well. How to filter. How to spot the red flags. And how to not keep picking the wrong guys. Now think about young guys. Most of them are the exact opposite. They get very little to no attention. On dating apps, almost nothing. On social media, almost nothing. In real life, almost nothing. Unless they act, most young men are practically invisible. That's why men are more like job candidates. And what is valuable, hard-earned experience for a candidate? Applying again and again. Getting rejected. Again and again. Failing interviews. Again and again. Learning how to talk. How to present yourself. How to communicate. How to improve. You don't become good at interviews by getting hired on the first try. You become good by failing many times. Until eventually, you get offers from one place. Then from another. Then from a third one. And so on. To a point where you know. Hey, I think if I want to be hired, I can find a job. That is the difference I am talking about. So no, a woman having experience does not automatically make her a red flag. And no, a man wanting experience before settling down does not make him manipulative or immoral. The real problem is when people rush into serious relationships before they understand themselves, their standards, their boundaries, and what they actually want. That is the message. Not, men can do it and women can't. Not, explore forever. No. Just don't lock yourself into something serious when you don't even know what you are choosing yet. And if that triggers someone, fine. But at least argue with what I actually said. Not with a version of it you created in your head.
